title: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

sense.text:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” When you’ve been in this truth long enough and seen enough, you learn where the doctrines inside the Israelite organizations come from. The rape doctrine, that the Bible allows rape, came from Edom. When people who hate the Bible critique it, the LGBTQ come with ‘King James is homosexual’, and when they can’t prove that, the next argument is that the Bible allows rape. That doctrine was produced to downplay the Bible and make it a book that promotes rape and violence, to move you away from it. Israelites who were not scripturally equipped to defend against it embraced it: ‘so what if the Bible says rape, we can do it.’ That’s how it was born. Confront them with ‘what if it was your daughter’ and they stutter and stumble, because they don’t really believe it; it gave them publicity and made them separate from the other camps. That’s a heathen Edomite doctrine. Their rendition of the Hebrew is nonsense.

The next one is the microchip being the mark of the beast, ‘if you get chipped you get condemned.’ That also comes from the heathen; they were the first to push it. Are there chips that can go in your hand? Yes. Is it the mark of the beast the Bible speaks of? No. Then the lunar Sabbath, that the Sabbath is based on a lunar cycle: a heathen doctrine. The same camp that pushed the microchip and the rape doctrine got it from them; three doctrines from one organization of Israelites, and all three come from Esau, from Edom. Then ‘we’re still under the old covenant’: also an Edomite doctrine, because the Israelis of today, who live in our land posing and pretending to be us, denounce the Messiah and say there is no Messiah yet, so we’re still under the old covenant. Do you see the pattern?

Then the black moon being the new moon, the moon unseen in the sky. For many years, from 2003, we followed the black moon, until about eight or nine years ago the understanding came out from the scriptures that the full moon is the accurate new moon. Bishop always said ‘I don’t want no dumb deacons, I don’t want no yes men’, so he sent me to the scriptures, not the books, to show him where the dark moon or black moon is the new moon. Day one, day two, day three, four, five: I couldn’t find anything. He brought it out in class and my mind was blown, and then I started seeing how it all goes together. The other Israelite groups cursed us out, and we said give us the scripture, and they couldn’t. Pointing to scriptures that have ‘new moon’ in them is not enough to show that the moon unseen is the new moon.

So why did we keep the black moon? It’s arbitrary: based on random choice or personal whim rather than any reason or system; capricious, whimsical, groundless, unjustified. By whose whim do we observe the black moon as the new moon? Edom, the heathens. A lot of what we think we know we do not know, and that’s why this was read first: not to envy the heathen, not to envy your oppressor. We envy him to the point that whatever he says becomes real to us. Esau, even the apologists, have gained such pride and arrogance that when they say something to black folks it’s true because they said it: ‘Christ is not black.’ How do you know? ‘He just isn’t.’ And our people are used to believing or disbelieving based on the arbitrary thoughts of the other nations, because we envy them; they’ve been our daddies and mommies and husbands and wives for hundreds of years, and we listen to them.

First Maccabees 2 shows that even the Greeks took notice of the same thing the Romans did. The history books show it first: Frontinus, a Roman soldier and eyewitness at the siege of Jerusalem in 70 AD, wrote in Latin that the deified Vespasian attacked the Jews on their Sabbath, which in their Latin is Saturn day, Saturday: a day on which it is sinful for them to do any business, and so he defeated them. They attacked us on our Sabbath because that was our rest, our weakest time. Cassius Dio, who hated the Jews and went off hearsay, borrowed from the annals of Rome and told how General Pompey took Judea in 63 BC, in the Maccabean period, before Rome had any power to give us a calendar: the temple had a wall of its own and was on high ground, and Pompey could not have taken it if we had defended it on all days alike, but the Romans battered down the wall on ‘the days of Saturn’, when we did no work at all. Josephus tells the same history: Pompey took ‘notice of the seventh days, on which the Jews abstained from all sorts of work on a religious account’, raised his bank on those days, and only then could take the city with its high towers and magnificent walls. What the Romans called Saturn days, we called the Sabbath. So we were keeping Saturday as the Sabbath for centuries before any Julian calendar; Rome never imposed a calendar on us.

“And Mattathias cried throughout the city with a loud voice, saying, Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me. So he and his sons fled into the mountains”: we ran from the Greeks.

The king’s servants heard that certain men who had broken the king’s commandment “were gone down into the secret places in the wilderness”. “They pursued after them a great number”, the Greeks pursued after us; “they camped against them”, they trapped us, “and made war against them on the sabbath day.” The Greeks made war against us on the Sabbath day.

“Come forth, and do according to the commandment of the king, and ye shall live”: you come out of that cave and follow the order of the king, we won’t kill you. “But they said, We will not come forth, neither will we do the king’s commandment, to profane the sabbath day.”

“Howbeit they answered them not, neither cast they a stone at them, nor stopped the places where they lay hid”: they didn’t argue, they didn’t fight back, they didn’t hide anymore. “Let us die all in our innocency: heaven and earth shall testify for us, that ye put us to death wrongfully.” This goes back to the MLK movement. They threw things at us, sicked dogs on us, beat us with night sticks, and we said let the world see how you’re mistreating us, and we gained civil rights. We were nonviolent: hold hands, go to them schools, throw food in my face, lock me in jail, beat me; the black man and the woman together in unity, marching, getting rocks thrown at them, spit in their face. Same thing here.

“So they rose up against them in battle on the sabbath, and they slew them, with their wives and children, and their cattle, to the number of a thousand people.” In our time they bombed the churches: they threw a bomb in a church in Birmingham and killed us, and many in Oklahoma as well. They killed a thousand of us, not defending ourselves, on the Sabbath day.

When Mattathias and his friends understood that these men let them kill them and didn’t fight back, “one of them said to another, If we all do as our brethren have done, and fight not for our lives and laws against the heathen, they will now quickly root us out of the earth.” If we take the nonviolent approach they will kill us all. So they took the Malcolm approach: by any means necessary. They used the Sabbath for our weakness, and our brothers said we don’t have no weakness, we going to fight these heathen. It’s the same spirit today: we plead to the white man and hope he signs laws for us, and we are still at the bottom. They will kill you and smile as they do it.

“Whosoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him”: we will defend ourselves. That would be your Black Panthers, and that’s why Esau went and changed the gun laws: these men got guns now, they’re dangerous, change the laws so they can’t have guns. “Neither will we die all, as our brethren that were murdered in the secret places.”

Later on we held the resistance and still lost, because the Most High had it prophesied that it would happen. The comparison is that the nonviolent approach didn’t help us and the violent approach helped us, but for a time. That’s why the Lord said ‘by my spirit, not by sword or might’: that’s how you win. Your swords and guns do nothing; they own the guns, the bullets, the drones, the nukes now. That time is long past.

“Then came there unto him a company of Assideans, who were mighty men of Israel”; “all they that fled for persecution joined themselves unto them”; “So they joined their forces, and smote sinful men in their anger, and wicked men in their wrath: but the rest fled to the heathen for succour.” The rest of our people ran to Esau for comfort: ‘oh white man please.’ That’s always been the coon. Coons have been around for centuries; they are a centuries-old being.

Read this regarding the words of that Roman writer towards us. He hated us to the past and made things up: that the Jews were refugees from a Greek island, which is not true; Greek and Roman mythology about Saturn driven from his throne by Jupiter, that we worship a donkey’s head. He wrote ‘we are told’, hearsay, that the seventh day was set aside for rest because we were lazy, and that in course of time the seductions of idleness made us devote every seventh year to indolence, which means laziness; they called us lazy even then. That seventh year is the rest the Bible gives: God says let the land rest. Others, he says, keep it as a mark of respect to Saturn, because our Sabbath day was the Romans’ Saturday; and he said our observances are sanctioned by their antiquity, that we kept them from long before Rome. All of it is conjecture. The one thing in him you can use is that many said the Jews are descended from Ethiopians, because we were black like them; the Bible says that too. Outside of that he cannot be used as a source to say we kept a pagan calendar.

“And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you”: they that hate you will be the Greeks and the Romans we read about earlier. “And ye shall flee when none pursueth you.” These nations really despise us; they put dumb history together about us that we have nothing to do with, and expect us to believe it because they said it. Same pride then, same pride now.

Josephus, against Apion, wrote that the multitude of mankind has had a great inclination for a long time to follow our religious observances: there is not any city of the Grecians nor of the barbarians nor any nation whither our custom of resting on the seventh day has not come, and they endeavour to imitate our concord with one another. We were the trendsetters; the nations followed what we did. A book published in 1916, ‘Sunday the World’s Rest Day’, says the Romans knew of the Jewish continuous seven-day week before Christ, finally adopted it to get out of the confusion of differing divisions of time, adopted the week of the Jew without his Sabbath or his religion, and when Christianity became the religion of Rome made the first day of the week the rest day: and thus Judea gave its calendar to the world. Rome didn’t give us their calendar; they modeled theirs after ours. Then “Behold, I have taught you statutes and judgments, even as the Lord my God commanded me”.

“Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” That’s what Josephus said. The nations saw these guys are wise, these guys are smart; the seventh day they have makes sense, the days of the week they have make sense; we’re going to follow behind them.

“For what nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them”; “And what nation is there so great, that hath statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law”? No other nation has those laws but us. That’s why all nations copy us. We are the salt of the earth: we bring flavor to everything we do and touch, and everyone copies us. The Arabs conquered us and made Islam; the Israelis conquered us and made fake Judaism; all the nations that came across us began to copy us while we were in exile and captivity.

This goes for whoever comes against this after class. There is an Israelite camp that keeps the lunar Sabbath and kept Passover in the winter, because they’re using the moon: keeping Passover with snow outside your window on a spring festival. Post up your feast day calendar, show us how you count your days and how you keep Pentecost; they cannot even explain it. “But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant.” That’s the conclusion: if after going through all these scriptures you are confused and ignorant, you’re going to stay that way till death.
Enough books; we’re going to the law. “Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” This is the introduction.

“Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation”. We kept this when Vespasian attacked us, when Pompey attacked us, when the Greeks attacked us. “An holy convocation” is singular: this is the Sabbath day in itself, holy convocation one. “It is the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings”: wherever you are, the seventh day is your Sabbath. That’s your seventh-day cycle.

“These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations”: plural, more than one. Verse three is singular, the seventh-day Sabbath, separate; verse four is the feasts, sabbaths also but different. “Which ye shall proclaim in their seasons”: these feasts are seasonal. The Sabbath day is not seasonal, it’s weekly. Passover never takes place in the winter; it’s a spring festival. If you’re keeping Passover in the winter, something is wrong with you: put your ass down and learn something.

“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.” The fourteenth day at even is the fifteenth day: the fourteenth at sundown marks the fifteenth; one and the same. Many who push this doctrine cannot count or read properly. Verse six is elaborating on verse five: “And on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread unto the Lord: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread.”

“In the first day ye shall have an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein”: the first day is a Sabbath. These days listed in verse four are sabbath days, but in their seasons. “In the seventh day is an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein”: the last day is a Sabbath. This is a spring festival: the first day is a Sabbath and the last day is a Sabbath.

precepts.why:
“These are the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations”: holy convocations, plural, going into all the feast days, and we tell the feast days by the seasons, and what we use for seasons is the moon. “To offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord, a burnt offering, and a meat offering, a sacrifice, and drink offerings, every thing upon his day”: all of these things we did on our feast days.

“Beside the sabbaths of the Lord”: beside the weekly Sabbath, which is different, as was explained in the verses above, with different offerings made on that day; “and beside your gifts, and beside all your vows, and beside all your freewill offerings”. It puts a difference between the feast-day sabbaths and the weekly Sabbath.

“Also in the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when ye have gathered in the fruit of the land, ye shall keep a feast unto the Lord seven days: on the first day shall be a sabbath, and on the eighth day shall be a sabbath.” That’s the feast of ingathering, Tabernacles, and its sabbaths go outside the weekly Sabbath. A seasonal sabbath is different from the weekly Sabbath: that’s common sense. Whatever you’re trying to bring out, make it make sense.

sense.text: “For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.” Not seven days, not a whole week: three days and three nights the Lord was in the earth, dead and gone. When the lunar Sabbath was shown not to line up with Christ’s death and resurrection, the camp got desperate and said he resurrected a week later, seven days later, just to make the lunar Sabbath fit. But he said three days and three nights.

This was buried eight years ago in the lunatic Sabbath class, and the necromancers of doctrine keep resurrecting it. “There was a man named Joseph, a counsellor; and he was a good man, and a just”. He “had not consented to the counsel and deed of them”, the Pharisees; he “waited for the kingdom of God”: he believed in Christ secretly.

Christ gave up the ghost; he’s dead on the cross. Joseph “went unto Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus.” He “laid it in a sepulchre that was hewn in stone, wherein never man before was laid”: his own new tomb in his garden. He put Christ there because it was closer, and time was running out; the sun was going down.

“And that day was the preparation, and the sabbath drew on.” The women from Galilee “returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment.” They rested the Sabbath day according to the commandment, during this week.

The lunar Sabbath doctrine goes by the 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th. Passover falls on the 15th day of the month, so under the lunatic Sabbath the first day of Passover, a sabbath, and the seventh-day Sabbath fall on the same time in that week. They would have had the Passover sabbath and another seventh-day Sabbath: two seventh-day sabbaths in one week. You cannot have two seventh-day sabbaths in a week; it doesn’t make sense.

So the new counter-argument is that when Rome conquered us they imposed the Julian calendar, and Christ and all the Jews kept Passover on a pagan calendar, and that is why it doesn’t line up. But we read in the historical sources that they attacked us on our Sabbath before Rome took over: we were keeping Saturn day as the Sabbath, and the Romans borrowed our calendar. There’s no historical record of Rome ever imposing a calendar on us; it’s not written or recorded anywhere. Why do they keep resurrecting it? Convenience. Every doctrine we encounter in this truth is a doctrine of convenience: you want weekends off, you want to work overtime, go to the club.

precepts.why: “Now upon the first day of the week”: the first day of the week after the Sabbath. “Very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared”. The women rested the Sabbath according to the commandment and came on the first day of the week.

“They found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre. And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.” Two men in shining garments said, “Why seek ye the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee, Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.” The third day: not the seventh day, not seven days later. Three days, three nights.

“Their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not.” Peter ran unto the sepulchre and “departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass”: where is Christ’s body, what’s going on? Two of them going to a village talked of these things, and “Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. But their eyes were holden that they should not know him”: Christ kept them so they couldn’t recognize him.

“But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel”: redeemed Israel, not everybody, not all nations; they understood that. “And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done.” Today is the third day, in the morning hours. So under the lunar doctrine they would have kept a seventh-day Sabbath twice within those three days. He was already risen by this time, and they didn’t believe he rose at all. Today is the third day, not seven days later.

sense.text: Rome did not give us their own calendar, and you cannot have two seventh-day sabbaths in one week. “And thou shalt set upon the table shewbread before me alway.” The showbread table is temple furniture. There’s a reason for going into the showbread.

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt take fine flour, and bake twelve cakes thereof”: the cakes are the showbread, twelve loaves. “And thou shalt set them in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord”: the showbread table. “Even an offering made by fire unto the Lord”: the showbread is an offering made by fire; you baked the bread by fire unto the Lord.

“Every sabbath he shall set it in order before the Lord continually”: every Sabbath they baked the bread. “And it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’; and they shall eat it in the holy place”: the showbread was to be eaten by Aaron and his sons. That’s the offering.

This confirms when the bread is baked. Other of their brethren, “of the sons of the Kohathites”, the sons of Levi, “were over the shewbread, to prepare it every sabbath.” It was hot fresh bread every Sabbath; the Levites were allowed to do this.

“And upon the table of shewbread they shall spread a cloth of blue, and put thereon the dishes, and the spoons, and the bowls, and covers to cover withal: and the continual bread shall be thereon”: on every Sabbath. The showbread is made and baked, set six in a row, six here and six there, freshly baked every Sabbath by Aaron and his sons and their children’s children down the line.

sense.text:
Shewbread, lunar Sabbath, new moon: where is this going? Everywhere. Many who push this doctrine cannot read it properly or count properly, so read the history.

David fled and came before Jonathan: “What have I done? what is mine iniquity? and what is my sin before thy father, that he seeketh my life?” Jonathan answered, “God forbid; thou shalt not die”: whatever Saul plans to do to you, I’ma know first. That was not true, but Jonathan believed at first that his father would tell his son whatever he planned against David.

David swore that Saul was hiding it from Jonathan, “lest he be grieved: but truly as the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth, there is but a step between me and death.” Your father wants me dead, Jonathan, you don’t know what you’re talking about. Jonathan: “Whatsoever thy soul desireth, I will even do it for thee.” I got your back, David, you going to be all right, I’m going to keep you safe.

“Behold, to morrow is the new moon.” Tomorrow is the new moon, tomorrow is the new moon: pay close attention to this particular history.

David should “not fail to sit with the king at meat”, but he asks to go and hide himself in the field “unto the third day at even.” I’ma stay in the field until the third day at evening; I’m not coming to dinner with y’all, your father wants to kill me; I’ma hide in the woods for three nights.

If Saul misses him, Jonathan is to say David asked leave to run to his city, “for there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the family.” Your dad asks why I ain’t come to dinner, let him know I got a family situation I got to handle.

If Saul says “It is well”, all right, no problem, cool. But if he gets mad, “then be sure that evil is determined by him”: he wants to kill me, and you’re going to know the difference.

“Notwithstanding, if there be in me iniquity, slay me thyself; for why shouldest thou bring me to thy father?” If I’m wrong, if I’m evil, you can kill me yourself; why bring me to your father to kill me? Jonathan answers that if he knew certainly evil was determined against David, “then would not I tell it thee?” If I knew he was going to kill you, I’ll tell you.

Jonathan sets a sign. When he has sounded his father “about to morrow any time, or the third day”, if it is good he will not send; “but if it please my father to do thee evil, then I will shew it thee, and send thee away, that thou mayest go in peace.” If it’s all good, I’ll call you; if it’s all bad, I’ll send you away. That’s all he’s saying.

Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, and caused David to swear again, “for he loved him as he loved his own soul.”

Again: “To morrow is the new moon: and thou shalt be missed, because thy seat will be empty.” Say it again. “And when thou hast stayed three days, then thou shalt go down quickly” to the place where he hid himself, by the stone Ezel.

Jonathan will shoot three arrows. If he tells the lad, “Behold, the arrows are on this side of thee, take them”, then David is good, he’s safe: “for there is peace to thee, and no hurt”. But if he says, “Behold, the arrows are beyond thee; go thy way”, the arrows are too far for you to find, don’t worry about it, “for the Lord hath sent thee away”: go on somewhere.

“Behold, the Lord be between thee and me for ever”: only you and I know about this plan, whether I shoot arrows in your favor or not in your favor.

“So David hid himself in the field: and when the new moon was come, the king sat him down to eat meat.” Now the new moon’s coming in. At this time, when the new moon came in, where is David? Hiding in the field like he said he would. “And David’s place was empty.”

Saul spake not any thing that day, for he thought, “he is not clean; surely he is not clean.” Maybe he ain’t clean, that’s why he’s not here: that’s what he’s thinking. But he’s mad he ain’t show up, because he wants to kill David.

“And it came to pass on the morrow, which was the second day of the month”: now it’s the second day of the month, because remember, the new moon is the first day. They had dinner more than one day, so Saul asks, “Wherefore cometh not the son of Jesse to meat, neither yesterday, nor to day?” Where he at now? Jonathan gives the excuse, “our family hath a sacrifice in the city”, he couldn’t make it. “Therefore he cometh not unto the king’s table.” This is day two.

Then Saul’s anger was kindled against Jonathan: “Thou son of the perverse rebellious woman”. He said your mom is rebellious, you evil as that. “Do not I know that thou hast chosen the son of Jesse to thine own confusion”: you stupid as hell defending that boy, “and unto the confusion of thy mother’s nakedness”: your mom is confused like you. He’s cursing them out.

“For as long as the son of Jesse liveth upon the ground, thou shalt not be established, nor thy kingdom.” You don’t understand: if this guy lives, you can’t be king. The Lord picked him as king. “Wherefore now send and fetch him unto me, for he shall surely die”: bring him here so I can kill him.

“Wherefore shall he be slain? what hath he done?” Kill him for what? What’d he do? Saul cast a javelin at him to smite him, “whereby Jonathan knew that it was determined of his father to slay David.” He’s trying to kill David, he’s trying to kill me too.

“So Jonathan arose from the table in fierce anger, and did eat no meat the second day of the month”: he got mad and left, “because his father had done him shame”, he was embarrassed. Read it back one more time: it is still the second day of the month. Those who say the new moon discerns the weekly Sabbath, notice: it says the second day of the month.

In the morning Jonathan went out into the field at the time appointed, with a little lad. Remember the message: if he tells the lad to go get the arrows, you good; if he says they’re too far to get, then you’re not safe. “And as the lad ran, he shot an arrow beyond him”, and Jonathan cried, “Is not the arrow beyond thee?” It was too far for you. “Make speed, haste, stay not”: don’t worry about the arrow, leave it alone.

“But the lad knew not any thing: only Jonathan and David knew the matter.” He didn’t know what was going on. Jonathan gave his artillery unto his lad, “Go, carry them to the city”: take my bow, my arrows, take them back to my house.

So far, this is day two. Remember David said it would be three days.

Read on into the next chapter: David came to the priest, and the priest was afraid at the meeting of David: “Why art thou alone, and no man with thee?” Remember, a couple of days ago you had the new moon feast, the day that, by their doctrine, determines the Sabbath.

David told the priest, “The king hath commanded me a business”: I’m commanded by Saul to come here and grab some food from you. David is starving; he’s been hiding all this time, so he wants to eat. “Give me five loaves of bread in mine hand, or what there is present”: what you got to give me for food?

“There is no common bread under mine hand”: I don’t have regular bread here, common bread is not here. Watch this: “but there is hallowed bread.” When is hallowed bread made? On the Sabbath.

Three days ago you had a new moon, and in their doctrine the new moon is what sets the 7-day Sabbath. Now you have another 7-day Sabbath, and the priest baked the bread on that Sabbath. This isn’t a week later; it’s the same time. “If the young men have kept themselves at least from women”: if you guys are clean, you can eat the holy bread.

“Of a truth women have been kept from us about these three days.” These three days, not seven. This is the third day: the new moon was the first day, the second day David’s place was empty, and here he arrives the third day, and he is offered holy bread that was made on the Sabbath day. That means the new moon does not determine the seven day Sabbaths. Everyone got it?

They will try to be sick and say no, that’s three days more: the two days of chapter 20 and then three more. Two plus three is five; that ain’t seven days, that’s not a week. Why you making shewbread on the fifth day? It’s seventh day bread. If it was seven days later, you don’t make shewbread on the fifth day of the week. Either way you count it, there’s no argument here: the new moon does not determine a 7-day Sabbath. It makes no sense.

“And the bread is in a manner common”: it’s common because you guys are clean; since you’re clean, the bread is common to you now, “yea, though it were sanctified this day in the vessel.” Sanctified this day in the vessel means it was baked that day in the vessel.

“So the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there but the shewbread, that was taken from before the Lord, to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away.” He gave him the shewbread made on the Sabbath. To put hot bread there the day it was taken away: the day David took it, it was hot and fresh bread, like Little Caesar pizza, pizza, hot and ready. That’s what it means.

So you cannot use the new moon as a 7-day Sabbath. Three days later another 7-day Sabbath popped up? That don’t make sense. And if you argue chapter 20 is two days and chapter 21 is three days, that gives you five, and you still can’t get a seven day Sabbath out of five days. There’s no way around it: either you’re miscounting on purpose or you’re not reading it properly, one or the other. Every corner is being covered.

Apparently the Messiah was keeping a pagan calendar to keep the feast days. “At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat.”

The Pharisees said, “Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day.” That is based upon their traditions, that you cannot pluck corn on a Sabbath day. That’s not biblical. You cannot harvest the corn, but you can pluck it all you want.

“Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him”: Christ said, okay, I’ll play along with you: what about the time David was hungry and the priest gave him bread they shouldn’t eat? Only Aaron and his sons can eat the shewbread, so how come they gave David that shewbread? He “did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests”.

“Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?” How did the priests profane the Sabbath and stay blameless? They start fire and they cook on the Sabbath; they make sacrifices on the Sabbath, and the shewbread is a sacrifice. So they profane it blamelessly, because they have to do it by temple ordinance. That’s part of the commandment, so they were allowed to pretty much break the Sabbath by temple law.

And it shows the Sabbath is separate from the new moon and the feast days. On the feast days, the new moon, the Passover, the public could boil and seethe and cook. On the seventh day Sabbath you could not cook, bake or seethe anything. So the feast days are different from the seventh day Sabbath, and the Sabbath spoken of here is the seventh day Sabbath, the day the priest gave David the bread: three days after the new moon. So the new moon cannot determine a 7-day Sabbath. Three days later another Sabbath shows up? It makes no sense. It is the same thing shown earlier in Luke 23 and 24: three days later, ‘today is the third day.’

“That in this place is one greater than the temple.” “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice”: because sacrifice will be done away with when the temple is eventually destroyed. Christ is the one who will have mercy. “Ye would not have condemned the guiltless.”

“For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.” Lord of what? Even of the Sabbath day. So is he lord of the pagan Sabbath day, lord of the Roman Sabbath day? He is Lord even of the Sabbath day. So they were keeping the Sabbath day properly; they were not keeping any Roman calendar that was forced on them. He’s Lord of the seventh day. The other makes no sense at all.

Let’s revisit it: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” This goes back to verse 37. When do you proclaim these holy convocations? In their seasons. You shall proclaim these feasts in their seasons, and the moon is what is used for that.

precepts.why: “From the moon is the sign of feasts.” A sign of what? Of feasts. The moon is a sign of feasts. It goes on, “a light that decreaseth in her perfection”, but the part wanted is that the moon is the sign of feasts: it is what tells the feasts that are proclaimed in their seasons.

It ain’t saying nothing new. “And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs”. Signs of what? Signs of feasts. Y’all got to be here and follow.

“And for seasons”: the moon is the sign for feasts in their seasons, just as Leviticus 23:4 says, feasts “in their seasons.” The moon is used for that.

“And for days, and years”: that’s the sun.

sense.text: “When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest”. The sheaf of the firstfruits is going into Pentecost.
“And he shall wave the sheaf before the Lord, to be accepted for you: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it.” The count to Pentecost starts from that morrow after the Sabbath.

precepts.why:
Jump to verse 15: “And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete”. You are to count seven sabbaths, and you do not need the moon to count seven sabbaths. All you got to do is count days: Sabbath, Sabbath, Sabbath. Seven sabbaths, seven times seven, gives you 49 days; seven weeks is 49 days, and on the 50th day you keep Pentecost and bring your firstfruits. That is Pentecost, and it takes place after Passover.

A pentagon has five sides; Pentecost means 50, the 50th day. Read it again: seven sabbaths “shall be complete”: 49 days shall go by completely.

Now what comes after the statement of verse 15? A colon. What a colon does: whatever is written after it elaborates on what is written before it. It shows a continuation, an elaboration. So verse 16 further explains what verse 15 just said. It is not a separate statement; it is one addressing the other.

“Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days”. The seventh Sabbath is the last of the seven sabbaths, the 49th day. Number fifty days: 50 days is Pentecost. You keep that 50th day as a feast: “and ye shall offer a new meat offering unto the Lord.” Some of us came out of the world as Pentecostals; that is not in the Bible, it is stupidity. Pentecost is the feast.

Now here is the doctrine they teach in this lunatic Sabbath: in verse 15 you count 50 days, and in verse 16 you count 50 more, so you got to count 100 days to keep Pentecost. Is it Pentecost, or something meaning a hundred, as in century? It’s Pentecost, 50, not 100. You count 50 days and then 50 more, and you guys are messed up: verse 16 is repeating verse 15. Trying to create their own day.

The lunatic Sabbath doctrine came from Esau once again. It comes out of a particular vile camp from which many doctrines stem: rape, microchips and lunatic sabbaths all come from that same camp. They got it from the internet; they got it from Edom.

In case anyone is still confused because it says 50 in that verse and 50 in the next: Deuteronomy repeats what is already written in the first four books.

“Six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread: and on the seventh day shall be a solemn assembly to the Lord thy God: thou shalt do no work therein.” Unleavened bread is what feast day? Passover.

Read on: “Seven weeks shalt thou number unto thee”. Not 14: seven weeks. “Begin to number the seven weeks”: you count seven weeks, 49 days, from the time you “put the sickle to the corn”, gathering the firstfruits.

“And thou shalt keep the feast of weeks unto the Lord thy God with a tribute of a freewill offering of thine hand”. Keep the feast of what? Of weeks. How many weeks, brothers? Seven. Does it say 14? It’s seven.

If anyone is still confused about it being seven weeks, see Tobit, who kept feast days in captivity. Those on that lunatic Sabbath ain’t keeping this feast day; you can’t keep it, you can’t count it using that moon stuff.

“Now when I was come home again, and my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks”. The feast of what? Pentecost, the holy feast of the seven weeks. Not 14: seven weeks. Pentecost is the feast of seven weeks: you count seven weeks and the day after that, and that’s 50.

They say no, 50 and 50 more. That’s 14 sabbaths, seven plus seven. Is it the feast of 14 sabbaths or of seven? Seven. Their count doesn’t make sense, but when you follow Esau you teach and repeat stupidity and confusion.

sense.text:
There will always be heresies and doctrines that rise in the nation of Israel, from amongst us or from amongst other camps. A couple of years ago there was a dumb, stupid doctrine that the Sabbath starts in the morning, and brothers and sisters left out of here following it, confused because they said they pulled 170 something scriptures. They fell back into the world and became nothing, and those teaching it bugged out of their minds; they don’t even keep the law no more. Now novices, young men who have been on the earth 30-some years and say they understand more than all the elders before them, come up with new dumb doctrine that the Sabbath is about the moon. These laws are not hard. Make sure you understand them.

These things got to happen concerning heresies, because some brothers and sisters don’t really believe. Somebody has to come and say something dumb and stupid, and you’re going to believe it and leave and go back into the world. Everybody who leaves over some dumb, stupid doctrine ends up back in the world, back in Christianity. Nobody prospers that way.

“With him is strength and wisdom”: with the Lord is strength and wisdom. Wisdom is understanding a little simple thing like the Sabbath day. When people don’t have wisdom, it is because the Lord is not with them.

“The deceived and the deceiver are his.” The deceiver is the person bringing that heresy. If you are teaching the Sabbath is in the morning, that’s a heresy and you are a heretic. If you are teaching the weekly Sabbath is according to the new moon, you are a heretic. But the Lord is working with you: the deceived and the deceiver both belong to the Lord, the one teaching the heresy and the one being deceived.

A heretic strongly believes in his doctrine because God has put strong delusion on him to believe a lie. Even with Deacon Eythan going over the weekly Sabbath, some following that lunatic garbage won’t get it, because a heretic strongly believes what he teaches. Everybody who teaches doctrines believes what they’re teaching is on point, and you can’t tell them nothing; they got a hot iron sear on their mind. Only the Lord could deliver you from that, the same as the Christians who fully believe in white Jesus and all those heresies.

There is nothing we could say to bring those brothers back. These lessons are for the new brothers and sisters coming in. The heretics can always repent, but the Lord has to intervene and take that delusion off them. So be careful, take notes, and don’t let nobody trick you concerning God’s laws: if you are a heretic breaking God’s laws, you ain’t getting in the Kingdom. It is not about not understanding a prophecy; teaching against God’s laws is destroying souls. That’s how dangerous it is.

Read it again: “With him is strength and wisdom”. Who is the him? It’s God. “The deceived and the deceiver are his.” Who is the spirit of deception? The deceiver is the devil. So God tells Satan who to confuse: go in his mind and tell him that the sunrise Sabbath makes sense, tell them follow that.

Have y’all seen any videos of them keeping feast days based upon that sunrise Sabbath? Not a single feast day or gathering: no Passover, no Tabernacles on a sunrise Sabbath. Because it was allowed to pull all the weak links out of the body, with some remaining, as there are always some remaining. That was the main goal: God said, Satan, go in there and confuse the weak people out of there, and let them grow more.

It all goes back to convenience. Those who don’t like keeping the Sabbath will leave and join them, so they don’t have to stress on a Friday and run to prepare; and when the day they say is the Sabbath falls on a Tuesday or a Wednesday, they still ain’t going to keep it. Everybody will heap to themselves teachers having itching ears, teachers who teach what is convenient to them: one teaching it’s okay to eat pork, one making up a day, novices teaching foolishness concerning the New Covenant, and brothers will follow after it. Our job is not to go back and forth and argue; our job is to go into the scriptures and bring out the proper understanding and keep it moving. Those whose mind is right will understand, and for those who don’t, remember: the deceived and the deceiver belong to the Lord.

“And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind”. These brothers and sisters, God gives them their reprobate mind; they don’t want to retain God in their knowledge. That doctrine was pushed so they could hit the club: the doctrine is for the club, mixing around with the wicked.

“To do those things which are not convenient”: see that. Doctrines of convenience.

“And Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, which provided victuals for the king and his household: each man his month in a year made provision.” He had officers who provided food for his household, twelve, each one for his month of the year: twelve months in the year. Solomon had twelve different chefs, one making his food for each month. He probably had all the tribes’ food: Judah made food for him one month, Benjamin another month. He ate every damn thing, he had it all, but he did have his favorite, Levi. Levi food is great.

In the Bible period the days of the week were not named by us; we had numbers: day one, day two, day three, day four, day five, day six, Sabbath. The day began in the evening, not at sunrise, with the appearance of the first stars. The Egyptians had a week of ten days and a three-week month. We came out of Egypt, and God said, no, this is your month right here, this is your day right here. Our week had its origin in the creation account, and it ran consecutively, irrespective of lunar or solar cycles: the moon did not determine the seventh day Sabbath; they are separate. The Hebrew month began with the new moon.

“And the Lord spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying, This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.” Why is Moses saying this month shall be the beginning of months? Another word for month is moon: Moses let Israel know this moon, this month, shall be the beginning. When you see the moon looking like this, that marks your month. The month begins with the moon, but the weeks run consecutively regardless of it; the new moons fall in the middle of a week and so forth, but it was a 7-day week regardless, the same as we have now.

Go back to it again after Esther and Nehemiah: “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.” That month is Abib.

precepts.why: He names the month: “This day came ye out in the month Abib.” After the exile, names adopted from the Babylonians were used, and on the Jewish sacred calendar the first month is Nisan, March to April. So instead of Abib, by the Babylonian name we adopted, it became Nisan. It falls primarily in late March, early April; that is when we count that month from the moon. When the moon comes up in those weeks, we know we’re in the beginning of the month.

“In the first month, that is, the month Nisan”. The month what? Nisan. During this time we were in Persian captivity, and we adopted the pagan names for the months. Of the month names on the calendar, some are of Israelite origin and some are pagan: Nisan is Babylonian; Abib is ours.

The same way, back then we said day one, day two, day three for the days of the week, and now we say Sunday, Monday. Rather than say Abib, we say late March or early April. We borrowed pagan names for the months of the year and for the days of the week, but it doesn’t change anything: it falls in the same time. Abib, even though it’s called Nisan, is today late March, early April, and that has not changed.

Abib means ear of corn. Why ear of corn about the time of our March or early April? Because it’s springtime, and an ear of corn sprouts during this season.

“And it came to pass in the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king”. In what month? Nisan: the name Babylon gave us, and we adopted it. Biblically it is Abib. So Esther calls it Nisan and Nehemiah calls it Nisan as well: that is the first month of our year.

sense.text:
Four sources now say the same thing. The Babylonians counted their sabbaths from their new moon, the 7th, 14th, 21st and 28th, and called them evil days, days ruled by the quarters of the moon; their last week ran eight or nine days and broke the seven-day cycle. Among the Jews the seven-day week was reckoned independently of the moon. The biblical Sabbath was ordained as a weekly institution with no relation whatsoever to the lunar cycle, and it is useless to connect it with the phases of the moon. That lunar Sabbath goes back to Babylon. Even the Babylonian rule that a physician shall not lay his hand on the sick on that day is where the Pharisees got it from, complaining about Christ healing people on the Sabbath: that talmudism came from Babylon and they brought it into our Sabbath, which was completely opposite to theirs.

“Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat”: when will the new moon be gone, that we may go to the club. Israel said the new moon be gone and the sabbath be gone because both of them independently are sabbaths, the new moon and the seventh-day Sabbath, and Israel did not want to observe them. It was burdensome to them, just like the comment that said how burdensome it is trying to keep the Friday Saturday Shabbat. “Making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit”: it is all for the money.

Abib means an ear of corn: the pre-exilic name, before the Babylonian captivity, for the first month of our year; after the exile the name was changed to Nisan. It fell about late March and early April. You cannot tell what late March or early April is without counting weeks: it is the last week of March and the first week of April. The weeks run consecutively, irrespective of the moon, and within that time frame a moon falls in between, and that is the month of Abib. That is what counting the month means.

precepts.why:
“For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” His commandments are not grievous, but to Israel they are. When it comes to convenience the laws of God become grievous to Israel; they don’t want to do it, and they try to find all kind of pagan Babylonian loopholes to go around it.

An example: you got a business, and the time you make the most money is Friday and Saturday, because everybody got the weekend off. The seventh-day Sabbath is from Friday night to Saturday night, so you’re like damn, that’s the time my business makes 50% of the money. Then somebody on YouTube says the Sabbath is not on the seventh day, you go by the moon, and you say that’s it. That goes back to itching ears. Y’all don’t fool nobody. God’s laws are not hard. You got to have joy in keeping God’s Sabbath; if it is grievous to you, you’re going to find ways not to keep it.

sense.text: “Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” This goes back to the rape doctrine: Esau trying to criticize the Bible, saying the Bible condones rape. Esau came up with that lunatic Sabbath. Esau came up with the shoestring things too, which are not in the Bible. Israelites start wearing them because there’s a chance in their mind we might be wrong. Envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways: none of his doctrines.

A lot of these brothers lack faith, because the Bible is plain: precept must be upon precept, here a little, there a little. Why is it so difficult for them to understand? Their lack of faith, something blocking the knowledge of God. “So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” See how simple it is: you heard the word of God, you just apply it. It is difficult for some because Satan is messing with them.

Anything we touch on, we don’t just bring it. When the Lord showed the Bishop concerning the moon, he brought it to all of us to make sure he’s on point. We don’t bring stuff to y’all without going over it, and that’s where the safety is. Heresies and dumb stupid doctrines come from novices: fatherless children, young men with no father figure around to counsel them and say no, that’s not what that means. The scripture says ‘not a novice’, a beginner, somebody new in this truth; if you don’t have a father or guidance over you, you will fall into the condemnation of the devil. Satan uses you to bring out dumb stupid doctrines to deceive the people. It happened in the past: the resurrection is past already; we’re not under the New Covenant; in Galatians they were bringing them back to the old covenant, to animal sacrifice. These things come from novices.

A side bar, since the shoestrings came up. “Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue”: right there is the rule of the fringes, the blue fringes. Fringes in the borders, all around the garment.

“And it shall be unto you for a fringe, that ye may look upon it, and remember all the commandments of the Lord, and do them”. So what do the fringes teach you to do? When Israel is scattered all over the world, we remember. The fringe symbolizes us being scattered into captivity and remembering who we are; that’s what it represents, and that’s why it goes all around the garment: we were going to be scattered all over the nations, and we would bethink ourselves.

When a basketball game is complete, how many quarters have been played? All of them: a complete game, all around. The four quarters are all around.

precepts.why: “Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee. Thou shalt not kill. Thou shalt not commit adultery.” Hold these laws next to the same laws in Deuteronomy 5.

“Honour thy father and thy mother, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee; that thy days may be prolonged”, “Thou shalt not kill. Neither shalt thou commit adultery.” It’s the same thing. Deuteronomy means Second Law: it repeats, recites, the laws found in the first four books, Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus and Numbers. Thou shalt not kill in Deuteronomy is not different from thou shalt not kill in Exodus, and honour thy father and mother is not a different law.

“Thou shalt make thee fringes upon the four quarters of thy vesture, wherewith thou coverest thyself.” This is repeating Numbers 15. The same fringes written in Numbers 15 are the fringes of Deuteronomy 22:12. That other camp says no, in the Hebrew it says tassel; but tassel is fringes, not shoestrings. It is not different fringes, just as it is not a different kill, different parents, different adultery: it is the same laws repeated in Deuteronomy, and that has to stop.

Nowhere in archaeology, after years of research, is there any evidence of our forefathers on this side of the world, in the Americas, wearing tassels, shoestring Nike just do it fringes, among the Native American garments. In Greece, in Corinth, a store had ancient Israelite artifacts of our clothes hanging up, fringed just like ours, not a single shoestring anywhere. Not a sculpture on a stone of us being carried into captivity in Syria, with beards and fringes, shows strings. One man took an image from one of our old books and digitally cut out the fringes so it looked like four strings on the bottom, but we have that book, and it shows the fringes all around. Any of y’all come in here with zizits, we kicking you out.

This is the scripture they use concerning the four corners. “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. When the Lord scatters us into corners, does it mean we are scattered only in the four corners of the earth, the east and the west? It means we are scattered all over the earth, among all nations. So when we read that we must put the fringes on the four quarters, it goes back to Numbers: the borders of our garments, right around.

At different times in history, according to the fashion of the garment, you put it on the border. Our custom was long garments, so we put it at the bottom. The North American Indians put it on the borders of the arm and the borders of their pants. And you put the ribbon of blue. That zizit stuff, don’t come up in here with that: that’s not in the Bible.

sense.text:
“And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws”. He thinks to change times and laws, but he cannot, because God says otherwise. He says the day begins when the sun comes up; God says no, sundown. He says your new moon begins when I say it’s black, arbitrary; God says no, that’s not what I said.

Who determined that a black, unseen moon is the new moon? Google only showed naval fleet websites. Asked of ChatGPT, it says the determination of the new moon when the moon is unseen comes from astronomers, from precise astronomical calculations: the conjunction with the sun, with the illuminated side facing away from earth, invisible to us. And the concept of the new moon was developed through ancient civilizations: the Babylonians, then the Greeks, then the Egyptians and Islamic astronomers. Hipparchus, a Greek; another Greek; an Arab; Kepler, a freaking Edomite. Now we know who tells us the new moon is a black one: Babylonians, Greeks, Egyptians and Arabs. Not a single Israelite on that list. Thank you ChatGPT.

That’s why Moses said in Exodus 12 this shall be your moon: the one you see, not the black one you can’t see. He would not have to say it if it were already unseen. This moon right here, bright and shining, that’s your moon: this is Abib.

precepts.why: “Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the Lord, the shield of thy help, and who is the sword of thy excellency! and thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee”. In the end our enemies shall be found liars unto us. The new moon was never a black moon: it was the full moon, that’s what God says. The day begins at sundown; it never began when the sun comes up. There were no tassels on each corner, as if we were scattered into one corner, Jews over here in one part of the earth. No: we’re all around the planet, and all around the planet we would regain who we are and keep the commandments. That’s what the fringe represents: all around the earth, all around the garment, all around the bottom of the dress for the sisters. “And thou shalt tread upon their high places.”

He shall think to change times and laws, but he is not going to fully change them, because the spirit of life from God is going to enter back into the twelve tribes of Israel and they’re going to start teaching the proper understanding. He confuses the world and lies to the world, but God will put his spirit back in his sons, and the Lord will show them the truth through the Holy Spirit.

“When he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, shewing them therewithal the falsehood of the heathen”. That is what we are showing tonight: the falsehood of the heathen. “And the breach of oaths”: the lies, the false promises and vows they made, breaking all the treaties with our brothers over on this side of the world. These are all falsehoods. The black moon, the unseen moon, is a falsehood. We told y’all this eight, ten years ago and y’all still ain’t listening.

sense.text: “O Lord, thou spakest from the beginning of the creation, even the first day, and saidst thus; Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work.” Now it’s going to get harder: going back to Genesis. His word was a perfect work. Everything in the beginning, from the first day to the sixth day, was a perfect work based upon his words: he said it, it was so, and it was perfection when it was made. Keep that in mind.

precepts.why:
“Upon the fourth day thou commandedst that the sun should shine”: when it shines, it is in its perfection. “And the moon give her light”: when she gives light she is in her perfection, when you can see it visibly. “And the stars should be in order”: you see them.

“And gavest them a charge to do service unto man, that was to be made.” Their lights are for the service of man. Can an unseen moon do service to a man? No.

“And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”. “And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.” They are there to give light upon the earth. “And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day”, the sun, “and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also”, the planets and stars as well. Remember they are for signs.

sense.text:
This is for every one of you that eat that turkey and all the leftovers. Thanksgiving is thanks-killing, the murder of our brothers. “But ye are they that forsake the Lord”: what makes you forsake the Lord? “That forget my holy mountain”: you forgot that you are one of the twelve tribes of Israel, you forgot that the North American Indians are your brothers, of the nation of Israel. You forgot who you are.

“That prepare a table for that troop”: in forgetting who you are you prepare a table. This is talking about the Thanksgiving table, prepared for that troop: Andrew Jackson, the US Cavalry troop that destroyed the North American Indians. The families always say we’re just giving thanks to God. No, you ain’t thanking the God of the Bible; you thanking the devil.

“And that furnish the drink offering unto that number”: the number of our people that was murdered here in America, over 70 million North American Indians. That’s what you are celebrating. America was established on bloodshed, and on that day you give glory and praise to the god of this world, to Satan, for giving the so-called white man the power to kill and murder your brothers.

“Therefore will I number you to the sword, and ye shall all bow down to the slaughter”: every last one of you that celebrates Thanksgiving will die; the Lord is going to kill you when he returns. So no turkey, no leftover turkey, no leftover stuffing in your mother’s fridge tomorrow. Wait till next month and make some turkey. When you do it on that day you are celebrating the murder of your people, and God is going to kill you in the end.

precepts.why: What troop are you preparing that table for? “Gad, a troop shall overcome him”. The troop that overcame Gad is the US Cavalry troop. That prepare a table for that troop: the US Cavalry troop that destroyed the North American Indians.

sense.text: “The sun to rule by day”: the sun, as in Genesis, rules by day. “For his mercy endureth for ever”. Why is David talking about mercy regarding the sun ruling? What does the sun ruling have to do with his mercy enduring forever?

“The moon and stars to rule by night: for his mercy endureth for ever.” What does mercy have to do with a sun and a moon shining? Ecclesiasticus, Isaiah and Jeremiah answer it: the sun and moon are bound up with Israel.

precepts.why: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.” The moon serves in her season, for a declaration of times, and the moon is a sign of the world. Remember: the sun rules by day, mercy endures forever; the moon rules by night, mercy endures forever. So what world is she a sign of?

“But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.” So the moon is a sign of Israel’s times, a sign of Israel’s time in this world: a world without end.

This is why the sun rules and his mercy endures forever, and the moon rules and his mercy endures forever. “Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar”: the moon controls the sea. “The Lord of hosts is his name”.

“If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.” If the sun and the moon cease to exist or cease their function, Israel ceases. The sun and the moon represent God’s mercy towards his people forever: as long as the sun and moon exist, we exist, and the mercy of the Lord will always be toward Israel. Israel is not cast away; if they were cast away the sun and moon would be gone. You Christians that say Israel is done away with and cast away don’t know what you’re talking about.

“If heaven above can be measured”, and it can’t, “and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath”, and it can’t, “I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done”. Esau tried it: go to space and measure it, he can’t; go deep in the earth, the pressure will destroy him; under the sea, destroyed. Can’t do it, because God’s mercy for us endures forever as the sun and moon endure forever.

sense.text: “And I will put enmity between thee and the woman”: thee is Satan. “And between thy seed and her seed”: Satan’s seed and her children. Her children shall bruise his heel, meaning they will conquer him in the end, and that goes into Esau and Jacob. The Lord is telling them what will happen between Satan and her offspring. Between Israel and Satan’s children, Edom, there will be war, and we are at war.

“Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow”: thy sorrow is the menstruation, the bleeding every month, the cramps. “And thy conception”: the labor pains they go through when they bring forth children. “In sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” The sorrow is the menstrual. Keep in mind that Eve is symbolic of the woman, Israel.

precepts.why: Who does Eve represent? “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” So Eve in Genesis represents Israel: the woman, the woman, the woman. That thought does not change through the rest of the class.

“Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.” Rachel had stolen her father’s gods and hid them. “And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me.” Rachel told her father, I can’t get up, I’m unclean right now, I’m on my menstrual, and she hid the gods around her. What custom is that? Go back to Genesis 3:16: the woman’s sorrow.

The law shows what her sorrow is. “And if a woman have an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be put apart seven days”. Her issue is her menstrual, and she is put apart seven days. Remember the thought has not changed: Eve is symbolic of the woman in Jeremiah 6:2, Israel.

Watch what it calls it here. “And if a man shall lie with a woman having her sickness”: her sickness is her menstrual, her issue, her sorrow. “And shall uncover her nakedness; he hath discovered her fountain, and she hath uncovered the fountain of her blood: and both of them shall be cut off from among their people.” He laid with her during her menstrual, he gets death and so does she. It is unclean, an abomination, to lie with your woman in the midst of her sickness, her sorrow, her issue of blood. Do not run the red light; it’s nasty.

Menstrual means relating to the menses, and menses in the Latin means month, because her sickness comes monthly, a monthly cycle where the body cleans itself out. Menstrual goes back to the word month: her month of sorrow, her month of sickness, her month of issue. And by law it lasts seven days.

“If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child: then she shall be unclean seven days; according to the days of the separation for her infirmity shall she be unclean.” “And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.” After the seven days, on the eighth day, she is officially clean: at the seventh day’s sundown she is clean, she takes the man child to the temple, they both are purified and offer sacrifices, and the male child is circumcised on the eighth day, making him clean. They both become clean on the eighth day.

“And she shall then continue in the blood of her purifying three and thirty days”: she has more impurity for the next 33 days, 40 days in all for a boy, and you can’t lie with her for that time; she has to heal. So: unclean seven days, the child circumcised and clean the eighth day.

sense.text: The thought has not changed: the woman is unclean seven days, and on the eighth day she takes the male child to be circumcised to make him clean. “And ye are complete in him”: complete means clean. You are complete in him, “which is the head of all principality and power”, and verse 11 explains what the completion is.

“In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands”: this is talking about the new bodies. Circumcision is the clipping of the foreskin; the skin of the child’s penis is removed, and that removal makes him clean. Circumcision with hands is taking a sharp object and cutting your foreskin off. This circumcision is without hands: a spiritual circumcision.

The first step is repenting from your sins and abstaining from sin, removing uncleanness from you by keeping God’s laws: “in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ”. You circumcise yourself spiritually. The last and final step is the Most High taking this unclean body off of you and giving you a new one: in the Kingdom this fleshly body is cut off and your new body is given to you. That’s the circumcision without hands.

precepts.why:
The body has to die. “But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come? Thou fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die”. This body, this flesh, has got to die in order to be quickened, born again. When Christ returns, those of us in this body, this body will have to die.

“And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other grain: But God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him”. God is going to give us a body. Those of us that keep the commandments are going to be born again, and the Lord will give us a body; we will be changed, circumcised without hands.

This is where Paul got it from regarding circumcision. “Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.” Stiffnecked is sinful. So the circumcision Paul made reference to in Colossians 2:10-11 is first and foremost abstaining from sin, and then, in the aftermath of doing that and maintaining it until the end, you get the new body: circumcised spiritually.

sense.text: “For my son Jesus shall be revealed with those that be with him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.” Within 400 years after Ezra, Rome will rise and come into power, and Christ will be born in that time frame, with the disciples that come after him.

“After these years shall my son Christ die”: Christ will be killed. “And all men that have life”: the disciples, down to the last ones, Polycarp and Irenaeus. After those two died the doctrine became straight madness. Christianity took over: Christ’s divinity questioned, he’s God, he’s the father, he’s the son, he’s both, it’s madness; the Trinity, Easter, Sunday worship. That happened after Christ died and those that had life died: the Dark Ages. When Christ walked with us we had light; when Christ died we ended up in darkness.

“And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days”: seven days we will be in darkness. “Like as in the former judgments”: there will be no prophets, and wisdom will be lost within that time frame. “So that no man shall remain”: none of those that have life, the disciples and the apostles.

“And after seven days”: what seven days? The context of her uncleanness being seven days has not been left, and the sun and moon have not been forgotten either. Remember: how long is the woman unclean, and when is she clean? After seven days. After seven days the child goes and gets circumcised, and that makes him clean.

“The world, that yet awaketh not”: the moon is a sign of the world, so this is the world of Israel, not everybody. If you awake not, you are asleep, in darkness, because the light is gone. “Shall be raised up”: they’ll be back in light. They wake up because they start to remember who they are, going back to the fringes all around: we start realizing who we are.

“And that shall die that is corrupt”: what is corrupt is the body. After the seven days you get a new body, circumcised without hands, on the eighth day.

“And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed unto them.” That is the resurrection, us being raised from the dead when Christ returns. Those that are asleep: we sleep when we are in darkness.

precepts.why:
When Christ walked with us, what did we have? “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men.” “And the light shineth in darkness”: Christ was the light that shined, and we were in darkness. “And the darkness comprehended it not”: being in darkness, we did not comprehend that he was the Messiah, or we chose to reject the belief.

“There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light”: John the Baptist was the forerunner, to introduce Christ into the world and roll out the red carpet for that light. “He was not that Light”: capital Light, going back to the light of Genesis 1. “That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.” Christ was the true light.

“As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.” What world is this? Israel. As long as he is here, you got light. When he’s gone, what do you have? Darkness. And what do you do in darkness? You sleep. Keep that in mind. The sun and moon, the woman’s seven days, the child clean after the circumcision on the eighth day: it is all relative.

“Yet a little while is the light with you. Walk while ye have the light”: walk while you have me, “lest darkness come upon you”, lest you go into sin, “for he that walketh in darkness knoweth not whither he goeth.” He’s lost.

“While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.” We are the children of light. We throw light here; we don’t do dark moons. You dark moon, you’re a child of darkness: that’s what the Bible says. Don’t get mad at me; get mad at your God that made you to be rebellious. We are the children of Christ, coming from Christ, the alpha of light, the main one. As long as he was in the world he was the light; once he died, what happened?

Once he died, and those that had life died, what happened to us? “Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee. For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. Gross means complete darkness: we were immersed in complete gross darkness, because Christ was gone. All that time we went into what is called the Dark Ages, and from there slavery and more darkness. Darkness covers all nations, but our people are in the deepest of the darkness.

“But the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” We start to repent and keep the Most High’s laws and commandments, and we become that light Christ spoke about, the children of light, and we start to shine in that darkness.

It goes with the light. “But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief. Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness.” The darkness, the sleep, the night, is us being in a sinful state, a wicked state. We are the children of the light, the children of Christ, so we should not be walking in darkness, neither should we be asleep. The people in the world out here are in darkness.

“Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober. For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night.” That is the darkness of Isaiah 60: after the apostles died the whole world went asleep, the old silence. “But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love”.

That’s why Romans says awake to righteousness. That’s why today the conservatives say they are going after the so-called woke. It’s not talking about these dumb stupid Democrats, nor these dumb Negroes running around with Black Lives Matter. It’s really code for us, waking up to this truth. They are targeting education; slavery cannot be taught in school. Even in society today they are trying to stop us from waking up.

“But the day of doom shall be the end of this time”: doomsday shall be the end of this time, “and the beginning of the immortality for to come”. The immortality to come is the new body, the circumcision made without hands. “Wherein corruption is past”: that which is corrupt dies.

“For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yea, perfect goodness and wisdom. The root of evil is sealed up from you, weakness and the moth is hid from you”: the moth is this human body. “And corruption is fled into hell to be forgotten”: what’s corruption? This body; it is gone. “Sorrows are passed, and in the end is shewed the treasure of immortality”: the new bodies.

“Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep”: going back to 2 Esdras 7:32, those that sleep in the dust. “But we shall all be changed”: circumcision without hands; that which is corrupt shall die. “In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed. For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.”

“So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.” That saying was written in Isaiah 25:8 and is found in 2 Esdras 8:54. Right now we are in a corruptible body, seeking the immortal one. When this mortal has put on immortality, death matters no more. Death was the judgment in Genesis; now we no longer worry about death, because we got our new body back. Christ too, when he died, had power over death.

This gives more clarity. “Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature”. Divine means godlike: you will take on a godlike nature, you will become a god, divine, celestial. “Having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust”: the corruption found in you, in this world, through the lust of the flesh. You escape it when you get that new body: when this is cut off and you get the new body, you’re circumcised without hands.

sense.text: Joseph “dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren”: “behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.” He saw the sun, the moon and the stars bow down to him. So who were the sun, moon and stars in his dream?

Jacob caught on to it quick, because he was a spiritual man: “What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?” I, the sun; thy mother, the moon, the woman; and thy brethren, the eleven stars.

So the sun, moon and stars represent a very important people, and it has nothing to do with the other nations. Now we know what the eleven stars are: the sun, moon and stars represent our nation.
“And his brethren envied him”: they hated him more. “But his father observed the saying.” Jacob kept it in mind, interesting, he caught on to it, and tonight we are catching on to it too.

precepts.why:
Remember: the sun is Jacob, the moon the mother, the eleven stars the brothers. “The sun when it appeareth, declaring at his rising a marvellous instrument, the work of the most High.” The sun declares at his rising. So the sun is a man.

That does not mean to go crazy and worship the sun. That is what happened to us in the first place: we knew what this meant, and we started bugging out over it. Jacob considered what Joseph said because he knew what the sun represented, and the moon too.
