It is a marvellous instrument, a marvellous sign. Remember Genesis, that great light: when the sun shines, that is its instrument in its perfection. And it is not perfect when it is going down; it is perfect when it is coming up.

“He made the moon also to serve in her season.” Put it beside Jacob’s words: shall I the sun, and your mother the moon, and your brothers the eleven stars serve you, Joseph? So the sun is the man and the moon is the woman, the husband and the wife, and the stars are the children.

And he made her “for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

sense.text:
Israel learned this long before we started going after other gods. Later we began to say literally that the sun is a man and the moon is a woman, and to worship them as gods themselves, but that was not what we learned at first. The Lord gave understanding of what those things represented.

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” Who is the glory of God? Israel is God’s glory. So how do the sun and moon declare Israel?

“Day unto day uttereth speech”: because they talk about Israel. “And night unto night sheweth knowledge”: knowledge regarding Israel. They speak to us by what their cycles say about us.

First and foremost, their very existence shows that we are still God’s people. That is the speech. As long as they are here, you are good with God; you get mercy. Remember, the sun rules and his mercy endures, the moon rules the night and his mercy endures.

“There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” The whole planet sees the light of the sun and moon, but they do not understand what they represent. God did not give that to them; he gave it to us.

“Their line is gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.” Paul elaborates on this: the line is the gospel, the word of God, the light, going with the children of light. Their line, their light, has gone out through all the earth, preaching the word of God where Israel is. “In them hath he set a tabernacle for the sun.”

It is no coincidence that the royal seed of Judah and Benjamin always work together: Peter, and then Paul, and what tribe was Paul of?

“Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber.” The sun is a bridegroom that comes out of his chamber, “and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race.” The sun is a strong man that runs a race.

If the sun is a groom, then the moon must be a bride.

precepts.why:
“I bring near my righteousness; it shall not be far off, and my salvation shall not tarry”: it will not take long. “And I will place salvation in Zion for Israel my glory.”

Israel is God’s glory. So when Psalms 19 says “The heavens declare the glory of God”, the heavens are declaring Israel.

“So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.”

Paul is making it clear that in Psalms 19 the sun and moon declare that the disciples would bring the light to all the ends of the earth, the same way the sun and moon literally bring light to the ends of the earth.

The disciples are the ones to bring the light into all the earth. They will not boast; the works speak for themselves. When the word is brought forth to the four corners of the earth and reaches our people scattered over the earth, they receive that light all over the world, the way the sun and moon give light all over the world. Who that is referring to, the class leaves for you to decide.

sense.text: “Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins”: that represents Israel. They “took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.” Who is the bridegroom? The sun is the bridegroom in Psalms 19.
“And five of them were wise, and five were foolish. They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them.” The oil is understanding.
“But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.” The oil is the understanding and the lamp is the commandments.

“While the bridegroom tarried”: meaning he was away. Remember, while the light is with you, you are in the light; when the light is gone, where will you be? “They all slumbered and slept.” So they were in darkness.

“And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.” That is us going out and teaching our people the word of God: the Lord is returning, repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. While we slept, now we start waking our people up. Repent, for the kingdom is at hand: that is what John said, what Elijah said.

“Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out.” They have not done anything; they have not been applying any commandments. “But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves”: go study.
“And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.” The door was shut to his chamber. They had a wedding.

“Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us. But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.”

“Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.” The Son of man is the bridegroom: Christ is the bridegroom.

precepts.why:
Who are the virgins? This is not talking about multiple wives for you thirsty brothers out there. “For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee”: marry the Lord. “And as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee.”

So the virgins are the nation of Israel, and the Lord Christ himself is the bridegroom. And in Psalms 19 the sun is the bridegroom, so the sun represents Christ.

“There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise.” The oil is understanding, in the dwelling of the wise: the understanding of the Bible. That is the oil the wise virgins carried in their vessels.
Now the lamp: “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light.” The lamps are the commandments, and the oil is the understanding of them.

The cry made at midnight: “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.” A voice that cries in the wilderness: a cry.

That voice is John the Baptist, who was Elijah. Before Christ came, John was the forerunner, preparing the way of the Lord.

“Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in: behold, he shall come, saith the Lord of hosts.”

This is the same messenger Isaiah prophesied of, John, Elijah, sent before Christ. And likewise, before Christ returns, he is sent again, to wake up those that sleep, that are in darkness, all over again. Here we are. That is the cry at midnight: Behold, the bridegroom cometh.

sense.text:
“For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven.” The day comes when the earth shall burn as an oven. That is heat, the kind of thing the sun does. Why? Because Esau is going to drop nuclear bombs, and where does nuclear power come from? From the sun.

“And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Nothing left of them.

“But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings.” Spell it: S-U-N, the Sun of righteousness. What does the sun do? It arises, with healing in his wings.

Once he arises, “ye shall go forth”, and grow up: we will be in the kingdom. So the sunrise represents us being delivered, getting out of here. The sun and the moon utter knowledge: when we wake up and the sun is up in the air, that is a sign that we are going to get out of here.

precepts.why:
“For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat.” That is Malachi 4: he shall come with healing in his wings, and when the day burns as hot as an oven, he will be our defense from the heat, just as he was in the furnace, when four were seen in there and one was a Son of God.

“And a cover from the sun at noon.” Noon is the sun’s strength, his perfection: noonday. You read noonday all the time, and noonday is going to be a special day for Esau. “A preservation from stumbling, and an help from falling.”

“The pride of the height, the clear firmament, the beauty of heaven, with his glorious shew; The sun when it appeareth, declaring at his rising a marvellous instrument, the work of the most High.”

“At noon it parcheth the country”: it makes the earth real hot at noon time, “and who can abide the burning heat thereof?” That noonday is the day that burns as an oven.

Where did “who can abide the burning heat thereof” come from? From Psalms 19: “Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber.” The bridegroom is the sun, with healing in his wings, “and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race”: he finishes his course.

“His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof.” Nothing is hid from the heat the Lord will bring. When the Lord returns, that is noonday: he is going to bring a heat no man can abide.

The same way the sun arises and parches the earth, that is what the Lord is going to do when he gets here. When he shows up he is going to deliver us, but he is going to burn people up too while we are being delivered.
Who shall abide the heat thereof? “And whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” Fire, the sun, and noon.

“He sent out of his mouth as it had been a blast of fire, and out of his lips a flaming breath, and out of his tongue he cast out sparks and tempests.” They were all mixed together and “fell with violence upon the multitude which was prepared to fight, and burned them up every one, so that upon a sudden of an innumerable multitude nothing was to be perceived, but only dust and smell of smoke.”

So the sun represents not only our deliverance, but what the Lord is going to do when he shows up during our deliverance: he is going to burn these people to a crisp. That is noonday.

sense.text: “Surely vain are all men by nature, who are ignorant of God, and could not out of the good things that are seen know him that is: neither by considering the works did they acknowledge the workmaster.” They started to forget the Creator of those things.
They deemed “fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars”, or “the lights of heaven”, the sun, the moon and the stars, “to be the gods which govern the world.” But they were not.

“With whose beauty if they being delighted took them to be gods; let them know how much better the Lord of them is: for the first author of beauty hath created them.” And if they were astonished at their power, let them understand “how much mightier he is that made them.”

“For by the greatness and beauty of the creatures”, the greatness and beauty of the sun and moon we are talking about tonight, “proportionably”, a little bit, “the maker of them is seen.”

What is Christ called? The bridegroom. What is the sun called? The bridegroom. You see a little of him, of his glory, in those things. They represent him.

“But yet for this they are the less to be blamed”: they were seeking God and desirous to find him, and being conversant in his works they searched him diligently and believed their sight, “because the things are beautiful that are seen. Howbeit neither are they to be pardoned.”

They are not pardoned, because they worship the sun and moon as if those are gods themselves, rather than the God that made them. They do not get off on that; the Most High is going to judge them for it regardless.

“For if they were able to know so much, that they could aim at the world; how did they not sooner find out the Lord thereof?” If you were so amazed by the creation, why not go back and honor the Creator?

We learned these things early on, and then we started to worship them. Everybody in this earth searches out what they want to be: to be a doctor you go deep, you search it all out. But when it comes to God, they are confused, ‘I don’t know where God at.’

precepts.why: “Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined.” God hath shined: going back to that sun, back to that moon. The maker is seen in the beauty of what he made, and out of Zion he has shined.

sense.text: “Commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.”
“And he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light”: as the sun, “and thy judgment as the noonday.” Noonday is your deliverance, and some are going to get death at the noonday.

precepts.why:
“Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.” Now you have an idea why we pray at these certain times.

In the morning we start rising, and by noon you are fully up: you are out of here, you are gone. That is why we pray in the evening, the morning and at noon.

“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress.”

“Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler”: that is the nuclear bombs, “and from the noisome pestilence”: the chemical warfare, the radiation, the diseases.

“He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust.” Back to Malachi 4:2: the Sun of righteousness shall arise with healing in his wings, and under his wings you trust. “His truth shall be thy shield and buckler.”

“Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” Noonday again.

Noonday over here, noonday over there. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” That is what we have to do before this takes place, “Before the decree bring forth”, before the judgment, “before the day pass as the chaff”: before the bridegroom returns from his journey in Matthew 25.

“Before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you.” It says the same thing as Matthew 25: virgins, gather your oil, gather your lamps, before the bridegroom shows up, before the day of the Lord’s anger, or you miss the wedding.

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth”: the Israelites, “which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” Hid under his wings.

“For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation”: Israel is going to be destroyed. “They shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day.” You keep reading about this noonday all the time, and that is the reason.

“Send ye the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.” This is symbolic, and it is also going into Christ. “As a wandering bird cast out of the nest, so the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon.”

“Take counsel, execute judgment; make thy shadow as the night in the midst of the noonday; hide the outcasts.” The outcasts are us; we are going to be there when that takes place. The Lord says they should hide them, but they are not going to do it. “Bewray not him that wandereth”: don’t push us out, don’t reject us from hiding.

“Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab”: be nice to them. “Be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler”, going back to the destruction, “for the extortioner is at an end”: that is Edom. “The spoiler ceaseth”: Babylon is gone. “The oppressors are consumed out of the land.”

“And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging, and seeking judgment, and hasting righteousness.” That is the Lord there. There is more to Isaiah 16, but for now, the noonday part.

sense.text: “If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him; If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.” Thy tabernacle is your body.
“For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear: Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away.”

“And thine age shall be clearer than the noonday”: clearer than the clear sky. “Thou shalt shine forth”: we shall shine forth. This is after the destruction. “Thou shalt be as the morning”: we shall be children of light; you shall have that glow.

That is why it was said to Isaiah, arise and shine: it goes into now, and in the kingdom we will always shine.
“And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety.” This is the kingdom here.
“Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee.” They are going to serve us; they are going to be slaves in the kingdom, making suit unto you.

“But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope shall be as the giving up of the ghost.” The hope of the wicked shall be as death. They will have no hope, only slavery and subjugation. That is their salvation: saved to be enslaved.

precepts.why:
Shine forth as the morning: “And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament.” Those of us that are wise, in the kingdom, shall shine as the brightness of the firmament, the same way Moses did, who had to wear a veil. That will happen to all Israel.

“And they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.” We are going to shine forever and ever, as the noonday itself.

“But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.” What is the perfect day? Noon is the perfect day: the sun at his highest peak, hottest, in his glory. Noonday. We shall shine the same way.

sense.text: Back to it, in case you got lost: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.” The sign of the world: that is it.

precepts.why: So the thought isn’t lost: the moon is a light, a sign of the world. “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.” World without end. So the moon is a sign of the world without end: Israel.

sense.text:
From the top again: “The pride of the height, the clear firmament, the beauty of heaven, with his glorious shew”. Then: “From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.”

She decreases in her perfection. When is the moon in her perfection? When she is full. She decreases when she is full: when she is new, in her glory, the way she was made. Her perfection is the perfection of her light, her glory.

Read seven first. What they do is read eight first and read above it; no, seven goes first, then eight. You failed eight years ago and you are going to fail again.

Why does she decrease from her perfection? Remember, the moon is a sign of the world, which is Israel.

precepts.why: How do we know the moon in her glory is when she is full? “Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again”: he was righteous, “and in his days fortified the temple.” In his days, during Simon II’s reign as the high priest, the temple was fortified.
“He was as the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and as the moon at the full.” The morning star: that is the sun. And he was as the moon at the full. What does that mean? Read on to verse 11.

“When he put on the robe of honour, and was clothed with the perfection of glory.” That is how we know: the moon at the full is the perfection of glory. When it is full, it is new.

Somebody used that scripture trying to contradict us, but they did not read it properly. It is describing the moon fully full of light, the new moon: full of light, the way it was created. When the moon is perfect, when it is new, it is in its glory. That is how the priest was.

“When he went up to the holy altar, he made the garment of holiness honourable”, because he was righteous. He stood by the hearth of the altar “as a young cedar in Libanus”, in Lebanon, “and as palm trees compassed they him round about. So were all the sons of Aaron in their glory”: like the moon at the full, like the morning star, at noon.

When you are full of light, you are in your glory. Keep that in mind.

Children of light. “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” “Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it”: take hold of the commandments, the Bible.

“Walk in the presence of the light thereof”: hold your lamps, like the virgins, “that thou mayest be illuminated.” Illuminated: full of light, like the moon.
“But the love of the Lord passeth all things for illumination”: illumination is enlightenment. “He that holdeth it, whereto shall he be likened?” He will be likened to the full moon and the sun.

“But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions.” Ye were illuminated: in other places it is ‘enlightened’, the same word. Enlightenment.
“O Lord, thou spakest from the beginning of the creation, even the first day, and saidst thus; Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work.”

Back here again for a reason: “Upon the fourth day thou commandedst that the sun should shine, and the moon give her light, and the stars should be in order.” The sun is the bridegroom; now we are going to deal with the moon, and her light.

Why does she decrease from her perfection? The moon is a sign of the world, which is Israel. “Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”: you were in your glory, noble and glorious, holy, righteous, new.

“How then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” We became degenerate. What does degenerate mean? When you go backwards, when you decrease. We went from being a noble vine, full of light, and degenerated into darkness. Now you are starting to catch on to what the moon is for. You ever heard the term? You all are a bunch of degenerates.

The sun, the moon, the woman in her sorrow for seven days, and the child clean on the eighth day when he is circumcised: that has not been forgotten. The sun represents the bridegroom, Christ, the husband. So who is the moon?

“Son of man, when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings.” We went from being full of light to full of darkness. “Their way was before me as the uncleanness of a removed woman.” How long is she removed?

“Wherefore I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it: And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them.”

So he removed us as an unclean woman, and we read before how long a woman is unclean.

sense.text: “From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.”

“The month is called after her name”: the word month comes from the word moon. “Increasing wonderfully in her changing”: she begins to increase wonderfully when she is in darkness, after she has decreased. “Being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven”: that is her glory, when she shines.

There are eight phases of the moon. Start from the new moon, in perfection, full of light; then she begins to degenerate. Going down, that is called the waning: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, and then waxing, until on the eighth you are back where you were before. Eighth day, you are clean again, full of light again. You start off full of light, go through that phase of uncleanness, the removed woman, and begin to wax, like that exceeding great army, until you are back where you began: children of light all over again. That is why we start from the top, not from the bottom.

What they call the dark moon is just darkness. You are using darkness to observe light.

precepts.why:
Now we read about her increase. The hand of the Lord set Ezekiel “in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”, and “they were very dry.” “Son of man, can these bones live?”

“Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live: And I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you”: knowledge of identity, the seeking of identity, “and cover you with skin, and put breath in you”: understanding who you are, “and ye shall live; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.” You shall remember yourselves. This goes right back to the fringes again: learning who you are.

“The bones came together, bone to his bone”, the sinews and flesh came up and the skin covered them, “but there was no breath in them”: no understanding yet, just the seeking of identity. This goes into the turbulent 60s, Malcolm, Martin.

“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain.” We were spiritually destroyed, killed. Then watch the increasing: “the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.”

“And after seven days”: seven days, remember, that is the time you are unclean. “The world, that yet awaketh not”, that was asleep, “shall be raised up”: an exceeding great army. “And that shall die that is corrupt.” After a while we are going to get out of here and get the kingdom.

Regarding the waxing, which is where we are right now: what happened with Christ is happening with us; the light is increasing. “And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him.” Waxed means increased.

The same with his cousin John: “And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the deserts till the day of his shewing unto Israel.”

So we are waxing with wisdom: that is the increase, going back to the fullness, to being new. The newness represents the new body, the circumcision without hands. That is the full moon: us in our glory, shining as the morning star, as the moon at the full, in perfection. The new body, the new moon: it is the same thing.

“These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth.” This goes into the two kingdoms, and also two figures.

“Fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies”: that goes to Elijah. “These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy”: Elijah. “And have power over waters to turn them to blood”: Moses. “And to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will.” We will gain that power again: as we reach that fullness, we are going to do the same thing our forefathers did.

“The beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them.” That goes back to Ezekiel 37, the slain, the bones in that valley: us being enslaved and conquered. “Their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”, Babylon, “which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

The nations “shall see their dead bodies three days and an half”: 350 years without knowledge and wisdom, dead, the valley of dry bones. They “shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves”, because it is spiritual. “They that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth”: we ruled.

“And after three days and an half”, after 350 years, in the midst of those seven days, in the midst of that week, “the Spirit of life from God entered into them”: waxing, increase. “And they stood upon their feet”: increase. “And great fear fell upon them which saw them”, because of what we are going to do in verse six, when we smite them with plagues.

That is the increase. “He that giveth his mind to the law of the most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.” He keeps the sayings of the renowned men, seeks out the secrets of grave sentences, and is “conversant in dark parables.”

“He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes”: he talks with the ambassadors, the prime ministers. That is what is happening with us. “He will travel through strange countries”: their line has gone forth through the earth.

“When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks unto the Lord in his prayer. He shall direct his counsel and knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate.”

“Yet have I more to say, which I have thought upon; for I am filled as the moon at the full.” Filled as the moon at the full, because of verse six: “he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding.” You cannot get around this.

Understanding is the moon, and it is at its full when the Holy Spirit comes into us: like the moon at the full, meaning when it is new. The moon is full when it is new. The heathens serve the devil, so they are completely opposite of us: they keep the new moon as a black moon, because they are darkness itself, and so is their god.

We are children of light; we deal with light. The one time we deal with the darkness is when the Lord said the evening and the morning were the first day: the day starts at night. But for keeping the feast days, he says use the light to keep my commandments, because you are children of light. He gave light for wisdom both ways, physically and spiritually.

After the seventh day, after that seventh cycle, you get a new moon. “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name remain.” The new moon represents a new heaven and a new earth, where we are filled at the full.

“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” We are going to be keeping the sabbaths and new moons in the kingdom.

“And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me”: those are the foolish virgins that did not have their oil for their lamps, “for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched.”

The Sabbath represents rest, eternal rest: no more work and no more oppression for us; somebody else does the work. In the kingdom we are going to be celebrating the day the Lord gives us rest.

The waning and the waxing: “How is the gold become dim!” What does gold normally do? It shines. It was light, and now it is not light any more; it is dimming. “How is the most fine gold changed!” Who is he referring to? “The stones of the sanctuary are poured out in the top of every street”: when the Babylonians attacked us.

“The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, how are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!” We lost our shine.

Now in these last days we are gaining our shine again. “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun”: as great as the light of the sun, in its original glory. There will be no more night, so the moon has no reason to go into darkness again; it will be bright all the time. The sun and moon represent us: we will be full of light, and likewise the moon will be full of light.

“And the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The bright sun and the bright moon symbolize the healing and deliverance of our people. The sun is the groom, Christ; the bride is Israel. Israel is the moon.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the light shall not be clear, nor dark: But it shall be one day which shall be known to the Lord, not day, nor night: but it shall come to pass, that at evening time it shall be light.” At evening time it shall be light because the moon will be just as bright as the sun, the night as bright as the day. This goes into the Lord’s return and into the kingdom.

“In that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem.” And “the Lord shall be king over all the earth”: that is how you know it is the kingdom. “In that day shall there be one Lord, and his name one.” There will not be a bunch of names; we are all going to know the name of the Lord and of his son, both their names, completely, no confusion.

“For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall change our vile body”: our unclean body, “that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body”, like that sun at noon and the moon at the full, “according to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself.” We are going to be new, like he is new.

sense.text:
The moon is a sign of the world, and the world is talking about who? The moon is a sign of the condition of the nation of Israel.

“For my son Jesus shall be revealed with those that be with him.” When Christ was born, the light came into the world. What phase was it then? It was full, it was new, because Christ the light came into the world. “And they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.”
“After these years shall my son Christ die, and all men that have life.” That life is the light of men: all men that have that light in them.

“And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days.” That old silence, those seven days, is us going into slavery, us not keeping God’s laws, the truth not being taught on the earth. Those seven days are us being unclean: the Lord is not dealing with us and the Holy Spirit is not in us. But the Holy Spirit is coming back in us.

“And after seven days the world, that yet awaketh not, shall be raised up.” Those eight phases of the moon: we are unclean for seven days, and the eighth phase is when it becomes a light again; we are clean, back in our glory.

After the gross darkness comes the phase with a little small piece of light: that is us, the truth springing forth. Then the truth getting bigger. We are at the seventh phase right now, about to go into the eighth. Israel is waking up all over; brothers are teaching all over the world. So the moon is a sign of the world, a sign of Israel, of us being in darkness and waking up. When it decreases they call it waning; when it increases they call it waxing.

“And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet”: meaning wisdom, her understanding, representing us. “And upon her head a crown of twelve stars”: it is like Joseph’s dream. That represents us as well.
